data.name: Frost
data.gender_notes: Frost is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'frost', meaning 'frosty' or 'icy'. In Norse mythology, Frost is a giant associated with winter and the frozen earth. In Christian tradition, Frost symbolizes purity and the coldness of one's heart towards sin. The name Frost carries the meaning “Frosty, icy, winter” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Frost usually hope their child will grow to embody frosty, icy, winter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of spiritual transformation through the coldness and hardness of winter.
